planting.note: Set rooted stem cuttings at the base of a sturdy tree, arbor, or lava-rock wall in constantly moist, humus-rich soil and loosely tie young growth in place until the aerial roots take hold.

directions: Ie'ie is a woody, branching Pacific vine found in Hawaiian wet and mesic forests, where it climbs tree trunks using thick aerial roots or sprawls along the ground when no support is available. Its glossy, spine-edged leaves cluster at the growing tips around showy orange-salmon bracts, and the plant carries deep cultural significance as the traditional fiber source for woven fish traps, baskets, and the helmets (mahiole) of Hawaiian chiefs. In cultivation it needs constant moisture, high humidity, filtered light, and something substantial to climb, and it resents drying out or exposure to cold or wind. It fits best in shaded native-garden plantings, lanai trellises, or botanical-garden collections in frost-free, humid climates, and is realistically sourced only through specialty Hawaiian native-plant growers rather than general garden centers.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in a shaded, humid understory bed with rich, constantly moist, well-drained soil; because the species is dioecious, keep more than one plant if berry set is wanted.

directions: Kanawao is Hawaii's only native member of the hydrangea family, growing through wet and mesic forest understories on all the main islands from roughly 1,000 to 6,000 feet elevation. Depending on site conditions it develops as a multi-stemmed shrub or a small tree, with large, leathery, veined leaves and separate male and female plants, the females bearing small clusters of blue-tinged berries. It works as a bold foliage and structure plant for shaded native gardens or conservatory plantings, valued more for its lush leaves and lineage than for showy flowers, and it needs steady moisture plus protection from hot sun and drying wind to look its best. It is not a mainstream nursery item; realistic sourcing means contacting a Hawaiian native-plant grower or botanical-garden propagation program directly.
